lf-deck.description: A pile of cards the user works through one at a time, like Slack's Catch up: each card is a decision or question answered with its own controls, an answered card moves on by itself, and Later leaves a card waiting until the end of the pass.
lf-deck.x-instructions: Write each card as a direct child, usually an `lf-ask` holding its question, evidence and widget, so each can be answered without the others. Put the deck's heading and any shared context before it. Order the cards as the user should take them. Use a deck when the user has several independent things to get through; use a side-list `lf-tabs` when they need to see the whole queue and move around it.
lf-deck.x-example:
Two things before the release

Which session store?

Redis already runs in production; Postgres removes a service.

Keep Redis Move sessions to Postgres

Post the release notes?

Post the 4.2 notes to the announcements channel.

Keep them as a draft Post them
